records.title: The antioxidant addiction of cancer
records.description: Antioxidant pathways support tumour growth, metastasis and therapy resistance while protecting cancer cells from ferroptosis. In this Perspective, Navdeep Chandel explores how stage-specific antioxidant dependencies can be exploited for therapy.

records.title: Beyond the tumour: circulating extracellular matrix fragments as next-generation cancer biomarkers
records.description: Through the action of proteases, the tumour-derived extracellular matrix (ECM) generates circulating ECM fragments that reflect dynamic tumour microenvironment remodelling in real time. In this Perspective article, the authors propose that advances in neo-epitope detection have enabled the use of ECM fragments as sensitive and specific biomarkers in clinical applications ranging from early detection and prognostication to treatment monitoring and immunotherapy prediction, complementing genomic profiling in precision oncology.

records.title: 3D models to capture and perturb tumour heterogeneity in vitro
records.description: Tumour heterogeneity drives disease progression yet remains difficult to capture in experimental systems. In this Review, Fomina and McGuigan discuss how emerging 3D tumour models, including organoids, assembloids and microfluidic platforms, recapitulate distinct dimensions of tumour heterogeneity to enable mechanistic studies of cancer biology and drug response. They also outline future directions for improving model fidelity, scalability and translational utility.

records.title: Origins and heterogeneity of colorectal cancer
records.description: This Review by Sphyris et al. discusses how the cell-of-origin determines the route of colorectal carcinogenesis and how phenotypic plasticity and heterogeneity shape tumour evolution, disease recurrence, metastatic competence and response to therapy.

records.title: Astrocytes drive stroke-induced glioma progression
records.description: Ye et al. show that ischaemic stroke can drive glioma progression through microenvironmental remodelling of tumour-associated astrocytes.

records.title: Single-cell tumour phylogenetics
records.description: Single-cell sequencing has transformed the study of tumour evolution by enabling high-resolution reconstruction of cancer phylogenies. This Review discusses the models, assumptions and computational approaches underlying single-cell tumour phylogeny inference, and it highlights emerging applications in cancer biology, patient stratification and evolutionary forecasting.

records.title: Hit the pause button
records.description: In a recent study, García-Gómez et al. identify an adaptive proliferative pause program that supports the survival of micrometastatic cells during early brain colonization and uncover therapeutic opportunities to target this state.

records.title: Cancer theranostics
records.description: Theranostics integrates diagnostic imaging with targeted therapy to enhance cancer treatment. In this Review, Sofias et al. discuss recent advances in radiotheranostic strategies, advances in nanotheranostic and microtheranostic platforms, and image-guided therapeutic and surgical interventions in oncology.

records.title: Lean, mean, breast cancer-fighting machine
records.description: Obesity is a modifiable risk factor associated with increased tumour incidence and aggressiveness. Curtin et al. identify an oxylipin secreted by lean adipocytes that suppresses breast cancer progression.

records.title: The urgent challenge of gastroesophageal cancer
records.description: Gastric and oesophageal cancers caused more than 1 million deaths worldwide in 2024. In this Comment, Cancer Grand Challenges explain how they have launched two targeted challenges to address this unmet need, inviting global interdisciplinary teams to apply for up to US $34 million in funding from the Torrey Coast Foundation and Cancer Research UK and move the dial towards the prevention of gastroesophageal cancer.

records.title: Mapping the functional dark proteome in cancer
records.description: The dark proteome encompasses previously undiscovered and uncharacterized protein molecules derived from alternative genomic loci or altered RNA translation. In this Perspective, Prensner et al. describe the current understanding of the dark proteome and set out the critical questions that need to be addressed in the field to determine whether the dark proteome can fulfill its potential for clinical translation.

records.title: Boosting CAR T cell efficacy in cancer with metabolic insights from design to diet
records.description: Although chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has advanced the treatment of many cancers, it is now apparent that metabolism is a major determinant of CAR T cell fitness, persistence and function. Here, Morgan, MacPherson and Lum examine how metabolism integrates with CAR T cell design, outline possible metabolic engineering solutions, and highlight opportunities to leverage diet to improve CAR T cell efficacy in people with haematological cancers.

records.title: Supercentenarians’ superpower to suppress cancer
records.description: Hashimoto et al. show that individuals who have lived to be 110 or older, known as supercentenarians, possess a high fraction of CD4 + cytotoxic T cells, which may contribute to the suppression of subclinical tumours.

records.title: Engineered models of metastasis
records.description: In a recent study, Chramiec, Baldassarri, Öztürk et al. develop a vascularized human multi-tissue platform that captures organ-specific metastatic colonization, microenvironmental remodelling and tumour-cell adaptation, offering a configurable system for modelling metastatic progression.

records.title: Psychosocial burden in cancer survivors
records.description: As health systems struggle to provide follow-up care for the growing number of cancer survivors, the psychosocial consequences of a cancer diagnosis remain insufficiently recognized and addressed. In this Comment, Patricia Ganz explores how survivorship care can better address the long-term psychosocial needs of cancer survivors.

records.title: From blunt-force treatment to precision: 25 years of transformation in cancer research
records.description: This Editorial marks the 25th anniversary of Nature Reviews Cancer . On this milestone we contemplate how our view of cancer has changed over the past 25 years and speculate on what the future holds.

records.title: Replication stress in cancer: origins, consequences and therapeutic opportunities
records.description: Replication stress drives genomic instability, tumour evolution and therapeutic adaptation, yet also creates exploitable vulnerabilities. In this Review, Chen and Zou discuss how chronic replication stress shapes cancer biology and how emerging therapies are targeting the pathways that enable tumour cells to survive it.

records.title: Viral mimicry escape as a necessary feature of malignant transformation
records.description: Viral mimicry is the activation of antiviral immune responses by endogenous nucleic acids that have accumulated in the cytosol. In this Review, Chen et al. highlight how cancer-associated epigenetic and transcriptional dysregulation promotes the generation of immunogenic nucleic acids, which can limit tumour progression. They further outline the mechanisms tumours use to suppress these responses, and the evidence that escape from viral mimicry is central to tumour evolution and a potential target for therapy.

records.title: Making breast cancer innovation deliver for every woman
records.description: Despite remarkable advances in our understanding of breast cancer biology and in the diagnosis and treatment of the disease, outcomes remain deeply influenced by where people live, how health systems function and whether care pathways are effectively coordinated. In this Comment, Miriam Mutebi outlines how we can translate innovation into equitable patient benefits.

records.title: A guide to understanding tumour evolution through the lens of population genetics
records.description: Population genetics provides a quantitative framework for interpreting cancer genomes as records of tumour evolution. This Review outlines how models of mutation, selection and drift enable inference of tumour dynamics from sequencing data, distinguish genetic and non-genetic processes, and support extraction of evolutionary trajectories beyond pattern-based statistical genomics.

records.title: Reflecting on 25 years of cancer research: transformative advances and unmet expectations
records.description: To mark the 25th anniversary of Nature Reviews Cancer , six researchers reflect on the conceptual advances that have reshaped cancer research — from somatic mosaicism, functional genomics and cancer stem cells to tumour metabolism, precision oncology and artificial intelligence — and consider which ideas transformed the field, which fell short of expectations, and what challenges remain.

records.title: A single-cell lens into the co-evolution of genotypes and phenotypes in cancer
records.description: In this Review, Izzo et al. discuss how single-cell multimodal sequencing enables genotype–phenotype mapping and, when combined with phylogenetic reconstruction, provide insights into clonal evolution, cell state plasticity, and cancer progression, revealing mutant-specific vulnerabilities and offering a framework to study somatic evolution across pre-malignant and malignant human tissues.

records.title: Neutrophils in cancer
records.description: Neutrophils exhibit context-dependent pro-tumour and antitumour functions in cancer. In this Review, Diehl, Basto et al. examine neutrophil roles in tumour progression and metastasis, drawing parallels with non-cancer contexts and highlight emerging strategies to therapeutically target and reprogramme neutrophil biology in cancer.

records.title: The next 25 years of cancer research: emerging perspectives and priorities
records.description: To mark the 25th anniversary of Nature Reviews Cancer , six emerging cancer researchers share their perspectives on the future of the field, highlighting conceptual opportunities, challenging established paradigms and identifying the approaches they believe will drive progress in the field over the next 25 years.

records.title: Expanding the reach of menin inhibitors
records.description: Megakaryocytes contribute substantially to the pathogenesis of myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), but therapeutic strategies targeting this lineage are lacking. Wen, Cotton et al. demonstrate that menin inhibition impairs megakaryocyte differentiation, suppresses myelofibrosis and improves disease features across preclinical MPN models.

records.title: The long return on discovery science in cancer therapeutics
records.description: Many advances in cancer treatment depend on discoveries made decades earlier. In this Comment, Murphy et al. discuss the histories of EGFR, HER2, CDK4/6 and RAS, highlighting how long translation can take and how clinical benefit can continue to accumulate as more effective drugs are developed, used in earlier disease settings and combined with existing treatments.

records.title: Early evidence of the carcinogenic effects of e-cigarette use
records.description: In this Journal Club, Yolanda Chirino and Estefany Medina-Reyes discuss a study that used mechanistic markers of carcinogenesis to provide early evidence of the potential cancer risks associated with e-cigarette exposure.

records.title: Shaping the future of early-onset colorectal cancer prevention
records.description: Early-onset colorectal cancer is rising globally. This Roadmap examines current knowledge gaps in risk factors, proposes an integrative conceptual model for risk factor discovery and prevention, and highlights the role of transdisciplinary science and patient engagement in reversing the trend.

records.title: Origins and consequences of oncogenic 3D chromatin remodelling
records.description: In this Review, Franceschini and colleagues discuss how remodelling of the 3D structure of chromatin in cancer is both a cause and a consequence of genetic and epigenetic alterations and highlight how chromatin 3D conformation might be exploited for diagnosis and therapy.

records.title: Brain barriers at the crossroads of glioma immune surveillance and immunotherapy response
records.description: Immunotherapy remains largely ineffective in gliomas despite success in other cancers. In this Review, Engelhardt and Platten outline how central nervous system immune privilege is enforced by specialized brain barriers that restrict T cell surveillance and discuss strategies to overcome these barriers to improve T cell-based immunotherapy for glioma.

records.title: Epigenetic changes linked to cell replication connect ageing with cancer risk
records.description: In this Journal Club, Sandra Romero-Cordoba discusses a study that identifies a replication-associated DNA methylation signature, termed CellDRIFT, providing evidence that epigenetic drift linked to cell division may contribute to oncogenic transformation.

records.title: An early shot at stopping PDAC
records.description: The progression of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) from precursor lesions presents an opportunity for cancer prevention. Haldar et al. developed mKRAS-VAX, a peptide vaccine targeting six common KRAS mutations in PDAC, and evaluated it in a phase I clinical trial.

records.title: Accelerated ageing confers early-onset cancer risk
records.description: Tian et al. conducted an observational cohort study utilizing data from biobanks in the UK and USA, finding that more advanced biological ageing compared to chronological age may be a risk factor for early-onset solid cancers with implications for cancer prevention and early interception.

records.title: Converging engineered models of cancer and artificial intelligence
records.description: No existing model can reliably predict how an individual cancer will evolve. In this Comment, Guimarães and Reis argue that the future of precision oncology lies not in increasingly sophisticated in vitro tumour models or in artificial intelligence alone, but in the iterative feedback loop between the two.

records.title: The DNA damage response and cancer immunotherapy
records.description: In this Review, Hong and Li explore how defects in DNA damage response (DDR) pathways shape tumour immunogenicity and influence responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors. They highlight shared immunological consequences across distinct DDR alterations, discuss mechanisms of resistance and evaluate therapeutic strategies integrating DDR-targeting agents with immunotherapy to improve clinical outcomes.

records.title: Who gets told what is impossible?
records.description: Twenty-five years after the launch of Nature Reviews Cancer , the experiences of women in cancer research have changed in important ways, with gains in visibility, representation and recognition. In this World View, Joyce reflects on the progress achieved and the persistent structural barriers that continue to impede equity.

records.title: Igniting antitumour immunity with cancer cell pyroptosis
records.description: In this Review, Liu et al. discuss how pyroptosis, executed by a family of pore-forming proteins known as gasdermins, can induce antitumour immunity, which might be therapeutically leveraged for synergy with existing cancer immunotherapies.

records.title: A viral coding circRNA contributes to HPV-driven oncogenesis
records.description: In this Journal Club, Muñoz-Bello and Lizano discuss the discovery of circE7, a protein-coding circular RNA generated by back-splicing in high-risk HPV that drives E7 expression and tumour growth, revealing a previously unappreciated mechanism of viral oncogene regulation.

records.title: Cuproptosis promotes antitumour immunity
records.description: In a recent study, Lei, Lu, Xu et al. identify cuproptosis as a form of immunogenic cell death that stimulates adaptive antitumour immunity. In turn, CD8⁺ T cell-derived IFNγ enhances tumour sensitivity to cuproptosis through STAT1–IRF1–FDX1 signalling, establishing a reciprocal immunometabolic circuit with important implications for cancer immunotherapy.

records.title: GABA takes the edge off anti-tumour immunity
records.description: Glioblastoma exhibits sex-specific differences in disease progression, incidence and immune regulation. Now, Pathak et al. identify GABA (γ-aminobutyric acid) as a key driver of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cell-mediated glioblastoma progression in women.

records.title: Escaping the trap
records.description: A recent study identifies TEX264-dependent nucleophagy as an important mechanism that mediates the clearance of trapped PARP1, thereby limiting PARP1-induced toxicity and promoting resistance to PARP inhibitors.

records.title: A genomic and epigenomic lens into the biology of acute lymphoblastic leukaemia
records.description: In this Review, Iacobucci and Mullighan discuss how advances in genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of acute lymphoblastic leukaemia have revealed molecular heterogeneity, lineage plasticity and mechanisms of treatment resistance in both B cell and T cell disease, thereby refining risk stratification and informing therapeutic decision-making.

records.title: Systemic health impact of cancer-associated extracellular vesicles and particles
records.description: In this Review, Wang et al. describe how extracellular vesicles and particles contribute to the systemic effects of cancer by providing a form of intercellular communication between tumours and the host through the transfer of bioactive cargo to recipient cells. These systemic effects include immune dysregulation in pre-metastatic niches, thrombosis and cardiovascular disease, liver metabolic dysfunction, glucose metabolism disorders and cachexia, suggesting that holistic approaches to cancer treatment are necessary to simultaneously target the tumour and its multi-organ paraneoplastic effects.

records.title: CLIM-TIME links tumour genetics to spatial immune architecture
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade, Weiwei Hu describes the development and use of CLIM-TIME, a scalable in vivo platform that integrates CRISPR perturbation screens with spatially resolved transcriptomic and immune profiling to link tumour-intrinsic genetic alterations to distinct immune microenvironments.

records.title: Imaging the hallmarks of cancer
records.description: In this Review, Grimm et al. describe the range of non-invasive diagnostic imaging approaches to monitor the various hallmarks of cancer and how their implementation is shaping clinical practice.

records.title: Serving sulfur to boost anti-tumour immunity
records.description: Gut microbiome composition and metabolite profiles have previously been linked to both colorectal tumorigenesis and immune checkpoint inhibitor responsiveness. Now, Lobel et al. identify sulfur amino acid metabolism as a microorganism-derived metabolic pathway that enhances anti-tumour immunity.

records.title: How to give a bad talk
records.description: Effective presentations require clarity and audience awareness. In this Comment, Itai Yanai outlines common misconceptions about presentations and how to address them to deliver more impactful and insightful talks.

records.title: Beyond oncogenesis: the unexplored benefits of viruses in cancer immunity
records.description: The study of tumour virology has traditionally focused on oncogenic viruses and their associated mechanisms of cancer initiation and promotion. Yet certain viral exposures can be beneficial by enhancing antitumour immunity. In this Review, Wang et al. explore the increasingly emerging evidence of protective roles of viruses in cancer immunity and how this knowledge could be harnessed to develop a virome-guided framework for cancer immunoprevention.

records.title: 3D multi-omics tumour atlases: from technology to biology and clinical translation
records.description: In this Review, Liu et al. describe the established and emerging tools for the generation of comprehensive 3D tumour atlases, the analysis of which has the potential to uncover novel biomarkers for risk stratification, early detection, preventive interventions, and transformative diagnostic and treatment strategies.

records.title: AACR 2026
records.description: The 2026 annual meeting of the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) was held under the theme ‘Precision, Partnership, Purpose: Advancing Cancer Science to Save Lives Globally’. Here, we summarize some key highlights from the meeting.

records.title: PRISM enables accurate microbial discovery in cancer genomics
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Bassel Ghaddar describes the development of PRISM, an efficient computational pipeline for microbial species detection and decontamination from genomic sequencing data, enabling the study of microbial associations with cancer.

records.title: Detection of cytokine-responsive cells using CyCLoPs
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Guangqing Lu describes the development and use of cytokine cellular locating platforms (CyCLoPs), a technology that enables visualization and tracking of cytokine signalling in vivo.

records.title: Mutation-centric kinase drug repurposing for rare cancers
records.description: Rare cancers remain underserved by precision oncology, in part because many oncogenic variants lack matched therapies despite a growing arsenal of targeted drugs. In this Comment, the authors propose that systematic, variant-level pharmacological mapping of approved kinase inhibitors can transform this gap into an opportunity for scalable drug repurposing.

records.title: An adenosine derivative for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma
records.description: In this Journal Club, Mauricio Díaz-Muñoz discusses a study showing that the adenosine derivative IFC-305 restores mitochondrial structure and bioenergetics while reducing tumour burden in a rat model of hepatocellular carcinoma.

records.title: Structural variants disrupt chromatin architecture
records.description: In this Journal Club, Stephenson-Gussinye and Furlan-Magaril discuss a study exploring how structural variants reshape three-dimensional genome architecture in cancer, explaining why only a subset lead to functional changes in gene expression.

records.title: Message in a vesicle: T cells boost tumour immunity
records.description: Extracellular vesicles have emerged as key modulators of immune responses. Hu et al. show that activated T cells secrete extracellular vesicles that promote antigen presentation in tumour cells and dendritic cells, thereby enhancing immune-mediated tumour clearance.

records.title: Beat it!
records.description: The heart is strikingly resistant to tumour formation despite its rich vascularization. In a recent study, Ciucci, Lorizio et al. identify mechanical load as a key barrier, showing that forces generated by cardiac contraction activate a mechano-epigenetic pathway that suppresses cancer cell proliferation in vivo and in engineered heart tissues.

records.title: Beyond sex determination: the Y chromosome in male cancers
records.description: This Review by Abdel-Hafiz et al. describes the current and emerging evidence that loss of the Y chromosome is linked to susceptibility, progression and poor outcomes in multiple cancer types, as well as its potential use as a biomarker for prognosis and precision therapy.

records.title: Mesenchymal stromal/stem cells in tumour initiation, progression and therapy
records.description: Mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (MSCs) influence tumour initiation, progression and immune modulation across diverse cancer types. In this Review, Garcia et al. outline how tissue-dependent and context-dependent MSC plasticity underlies their tumour-supportive or tumour-restraining functions and highlight emerging mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities that position MSC biology as a promising avenue for cancer treatment.

records.title: Tracing disease origin with plasma cell-free chromatin
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Xiaoxuan Meng describes the development of cf-EpiTracing, a highly sensitive and automated epigenetic liquid-biopsy platform that captures histone modifications on cell-free chromatin from plasma, enabling unbiased monitoring of cancer.

records.title: Regulation of immune checkpoint molecules in cancer immune evasion and therapy
records.description: Tumours evade immunity by dynamically rewiring immune checkpoint expression across multiple regulatory layers. In this Review, Eris, Zu et al. synthesize how these mechanisms operate in tumour and immune cells, connect them to therapeutic resistance, and highlight emerging biomarkers and therapeutic strategies that target convergent regulatory nodes to improve immunotherapy outcomes.

records.title: Remembering inflammation increases cancer risk
records.description: Colitis predisposes to colorectal cancer, but how inflammation promotes tumour initiation has remained unclear. Nagaraja et al. show that inflammatory injury imprints a heritable epigenetic memory in colonic stem cells that enhances AP-1-driven proliferative programs and accelerates malignant outgrowth following oncogenic mutation.

records.title: Stem cells as an essential mediator of the exercise–tumorigenesis link
records.description: Aerobic exercise influences physiology and generally reduces cancer risk, yet the mechanisms connecting these effects remain incompletely understood. In this Perspective, Zhuang and colleagues outline a model in which exercise-induced physiological adaptation regulates adult stem cell behaviour in ways that limit transformation and tumour initiation.

records.title: Microplastics but macro-concerns on the brain
records.description: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly recognized as pervasive environmental exposures. Li et al. analysed human brain tumour samples and post-mortem healthy brain tissue to quantify MNP burden, and characterize particle composition and spatial distribution.

records.title: The sleeping threat: targeting cancer dormancy to transform metastasis therapy
records.description: This Review synthesizes emerging insights into how microenvironmental cues, epigenetic programmes and immune interactions govern disseminated cancer cell dormancy and outlines how advances in dormancy research could guide the development of biomarkers and therapies to prevent metastatic relapse.

records.title: Enhancer and metabolic rewiring by KMT2C–COMPASS or KMT2D–COMPASS family loss in cancer creates druggable vulnerabilities
records.description: In this Review, Zhao and Shilatifard examine how mutations in components of the KMT2C-containing or KMT2D-containing COMPASS complex drive cancer progression and discuss therapeutic approaches targeting epigenetic, metabolic, immune and DNA repair vulnerabilities arising from this altered COMPASS activity.

records.title: Context-dependent synthetic lethality — an emerging precision therapeutic approach
records.description: In this Review, Chang et al. discuss context-dependent synthetic lethality whereby various genetic contexts produce cancer-intrinsic vulnerabilities and provide a framework that evaluates and considers therapeutic index to enable the translation of synthetic lethality into more selective and durable cancer therapies.

records.title: Cancer risk in children with congenital anomalies
records.description: The established link between congenital anomalies and cancer could lead to improved surveillance and therapeutic strategies. However, we must first expand population-based studies to confirm these patterns, along with detailed molecular assessments to identify risk markers and deeper patient profiling to support precision medicine.

records.title: Advancing AI for multi-omics and clinical data integration in basic and translational cancer research
records.description: While high-throughput omics have deepened our understanding of tumour complexity, analyses restricted to a single omics layer risk overlooking key dimensions of biological regulation. In this Review, Liu and colleagues highlight how artificial intelligence could be harnessed for integrating multi-omics data to provide patient-specific insights into cancer mechanisms and treatment response.

records.title: Microbiota and immune-related adverse events in cancer immunotherapy
records.description: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) complicate cancer immunotherapy, necessitating cancer treatment cessation and management of irAEs. In this Progress article, Schneider et al. highlight the role of the microbiome in driving irAE development and progression, particularly immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated colitis, through clinical and preclinical evidence, emphasizing immune and microbial interactions while discussing potential therapeutic strategies to mitigate risks.

records.title: vCATCH enables body-wide in vivo drug distribution mapping
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Zhengyuan Pang describes the development and use of volumetric clearing-assisted tissue click chemistry (vCATCH), a pipeline that enables mapping of covalent drug binding at cellular resolution across a mouse body.

records.title: The versatile interplay between steatotic liver disease and liver cancer
records.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and alcoholic liver disease (ALD) are drivers of liver cancer, promoting its development through chronic liver injury and inflammation. In this Review, Rahbari et al. highlight the distinct pathophysiological mechanisms of progression and therapeutic advancements for MASLD and ALD, emphasizing the need for more tailored approaches to manage these complex diseases and their cancer risks.

records.title: Rethinking ovarian cancer III: the past decade and future directions
records.description: In this Expert Recommendation, Bowtell and colleagues outline progress made over the last decade in the research and treatment of high-grade serous carcinoma as well as current challenges and research priorities for the coming years to reduce incidence and improve patient outcomes.

records.title: Kill three birds with one stone
records.description: In a recent study, Gudenas et al. map pineoblastoma subgroups to pinealocyte progenitors and identify a shared photoreceptor-like transcriptional network across pineoblastoma, retinoblastoma and group 3 medulloblastoma, revealing a developmental vulnerability with therapeutic potential.

records.title: A fatty competitor in tumour immunity
records.description: Adipose tissue and adipocytes have been implicated in promoting tumour progression and hindering anti-tumour immunity. Wang et al. investigated the functional role of tumour-associated visceral adipose tissue in regulating colorectal cancer anti-tumour immunity and immunotherapy efficacy.

records.title: Targeting shared neoantigens in solid tumours
records.description: In this Journal Club, Terrazas and Peón discuss a study that identifies a recurrent CTNNB1 mutation that generates shared neoantigens amenable to engineered T cell receptor (TCR)-T cell recognition. The work demonstrates potent antitumour activity across models and highlights the potential of targeting public mutations to broaden TCR-T cell immunotherapy for solid tumours.

records.title: AI-driven smart patient retrieval for precision oncology
records.description: Tumour boards are often constrained by time-intensive data preparation and discussion. In this Comment, Wang and Chaudhari advocate for the use of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven smart patient-retrieval systems to facilitate more informed and individualized clinical decision-making.

records.title: Functional m 6 A site detection by FOCAS
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yifan Zhang describes the development and use of FOCAS, a platform for site-specific, transcriptome-wide mapping of functional m 6 A RNA modifications, revealing widespread intra-transcript functional diversity and uncovering epitranscriptomic and epigenomic interactions that shape cancer cell fitness.

records.title: Striking the right balance with type I interferon signalling in cancer
records.description: Type I interferons (IFNs) critically influence cancer development, progression and therapeutic response. In this Review, Parker, Haynes and colleagues explore the complexity of IFN signalling, with a particular focus on tumour-intrinsic mechanisms, and outline strategies for reprogramming IFN activity in tumours to enhance anticancer immunity and improve patient outcomes.

records.title: Avoiding cancer through collective behaviour
records.description: In this Journal Club, Rodríguez-Lelis and Gómez-Schiavon discuss a study that challenges the oncogene-induced senescence paradigm and proposes that cooperative, feedback-driven growth arrest better explains growth dynamics in BRAF-mutant benign nevi.

records.title: Metabolic vulnerability in fusion-driven ependymoma
records.description: In a recent study published in Nature , Natarajan et al. uncover a metabolic–epigenetic circuit in which glutamine-derived itaconate functions as an oncometabolite to sustain oncogenic ZFTA–RELA expression in ependymoma. Disrupting this pathway lowers ZFTA–RELA levels and suppresses tumour growth in preclinical models, revealing a promising therapeutic vulnerability in this aggressive cancer.

records.title: Re-routing IgE for cancer therapy
records.description: In a study published in Cell , Xu et al. show that mast cells engineered with tumour-antigen specific antibodies and loaded with an oncolytic virus can be activated by antigen encounter to drive targeted tumour cell killing and amplify local anti-tumour immunity.

records.title: Claudin proteins as emerging therapeutic targets for solid tumours
records.description: In this Review, Saviano et al. explore the frequent deregulation of claudins (CLDNs) in solid tumours and highlight their role in cancer progression. They discuss strategies to target CLDNs by exploiting tumour-specific surface expression or inhibiting oncogenic signalling and outline knowledge gaps, challenges and opportunities for advancing CLDN-directed cancer therapies.

records.title: The intestinal microbiota as a key modulator of acute graft-versus-host disease
records.description: In this Review, Paredes et al. discuss preclinical and clinical evidence suggesting that the intestinal microbiome influences outcomes of allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation and, in particular, graft-versus-host disease and propose that microbiota-focused approaches may improve these clinical outcomes.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-generated synthetic data for cancer research and clinical trials
records.description: Synthetic data generated by generative artificial intelligence models can serve as a substitute for real patient data. In this Review, Eckardt et al. discuss how synthetic data sets can overcome barriers to data access and sharing, democratize scientific discovery in cancer research, and reduce the costs and failure rates of cancer clinical trials. They also discuss how this will only become possible if we can overcome the challenges of a lack of standardization in training data selection, model evaluation, bias mitigation, privacy preservation and quality assurance.

records.title: Decoding cancer across scales with metabolomics
records.description: In this Review, Rowles and Patti present metabolomics workflows to study cancer across scales. They explore the nutrient demands of cancer cells and how those needs can be fulfilled through metabolic interactions within the tumour microenvironment or systemic crosstalk with distant tissues, and discuss the opportunities and challenges of each approach and offer insights into future research directions.

records.title: Inherited resilience
records.description: Mutant haematopoietic stem cells display broad fitness variation, suggesting that protective mechanisms may limit clonal expansion and malignant transformation. Now, Agarwal et al. identify a germline noncoding variant that confers resilience to clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) by dampening expression of the RNA-binding protein MSI2.

records.title: Carboplatin trains macrophages for cardiac defence
records.description: In a recent Science Immunology paper, He et al. show that treatment with the chemotherapy carboplatin reshapes cardiac-resident macrophage populations, protecting against later heart disease.

records.title: l -Fucose: a dietary sugar with multifaceted potential in the biology and therapy of cancer
records.description: The conjugation of glycoproteins and glycolipids with the dietary sugar L -fucose is known as fucosylation. In this Progress article, Bitaraf et al. describe the latest work showing how fucosylation is deregulated in cancer, influencing tumour progression and therapeutic responses, and how it might be leveraged to treat cancer.

records.title: Cat viruses as windows into human oncogenesis
records.description: Oncogenic viruses cause 15% of all human cancers. Cats, which are naturally susceptible to cancers caused by feline homologues of human tumour viruses, represent an opportunity to develop treatment and prevention strategies for viral cancers using comparative oncology. Increased investment in this approach could benefit both pets and people.

records.title: Radiation as an immune modulator: mechanisms and implications for combination with immunotherapy
records.description: Radiation therapy induces immune responses both systemically and within the tumour microenvironment. In this Review, Darragh and Karam present preclinical and clinical evidence to highlight this complex interplay and outline strategies to enhance the immunogenic potential of radiation therapy to improve both therapeutic efficacy and patient outcomes.

records.title: Tumour explants as next-generation models of cancer
records.description: To preserve tumour architecture, cellular heterogeneity and the dynamic crosstalk that influences cancer, Fong and colleagues advocate for coordinated, cross-disciplinary and sustained efforts to promote the widespread adoption of tumour explants.

records.title: The rise of spatial insights into tumour tissue architecture
records.description: In this Journal Club, Siliceo and Rodríguez discuss a study that presents histoCAT, an interactive toolbox for spatial biology that combines image-based visualization with unsupervised cellular neighborhood analysis to uncover tissue architecture and cell–cell interactions.

records.title: Heterocellular crosstalk and architecture of the pancreatic tumour microenvironment
records.description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is defined by a fibroinflammatory microenvironment, which influences both disease progression and therapy response. In this Review, Arnold et al. outline our current understanding of the complex interplay between the stromal elements of the tumour microenvironment in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and present ways we might use this knowledge to develop better therapeutic strategies for patients with pancreatic cancer.

records.title: Artificial intelligence agents in cancer research and oncology
records.description: Artificial intelligence agents are autonomous systems that use large language models to reason and as such can perform complex, multistep tasks with minimal human oversight. This Review by Truhn et al. discusses how these agents — which have already been implemented in several industries — could transform cancer research and oncology, and looks at the challenges that need to be addressed before they can be efficiently and safely used.

records.title: When the time is right
records.description: In a study published in Nature , Lourenço et al. demonstrate that strong oncogenic driver mutations undergo negative selection unless they occur in a permissive tissue context.

records.title: Opportunities and challenges of targeting cGAS–STING in cancer
records.description: In this Review, Lu et al. discuss the dual role of the cyclic guanosine monophosphate–adenosine monophosphate synthase (cGAS)–stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway in cancer, emphasizing its involvement in both tumour suppression and promotion. They highlight the diverse sources of pathway activation and suggest that this functional duality may underlie the limited clinical success of cGAS–STING targeting in cancer therapy.

records.title: Double trouble for the tumour glycocode
records.description: By incorporating lectins that target specific tumour-associated carbohydrate antigens, Zhou et al. engineered bispecific antibodies that induce effective T cell activation and tumour regression in various cancers.

records.title: Convergence of machine learning and genomics for precision oncology
records.description: In this Perspective, Reardon et al. explore how integrating machine learning into next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based molecular diagnostic workflows can enhance precision oncology. They discuss the benefits, challenges and responsible implementation of these approaches, highlighting their potential to streamline variant interpretation, maximize clinical insights and support more informed decision-making at the point-of-care.

records.title: The antioxidant addiction of cancer
records.description: Antioxidant pathways support tumour growth, metastasis and therapy resistance while protecting cancer cells from ferroptosis. In this Perspective, Navdeep Chandel explores how stage-specific antioxidant dependencies can be exploited for therapy.

records.title: Beyond the tumour: circulating extracellular matrix fragments as next-generation cancer biomarkers
records.description: Through the action of proteases, the tumour-derived extracellular matrix (ECM) generates circulating ECM fragments that reflect dynamic tumour microenvironment remodelling in real time. In this Perspective article, the authors propose that advances in neo-epitope detection have enabled the use of ECM fragments as sensitive and specific biomarkers in clinical applications ranging from early detection and prognostication to treatment monitoring and immunotherapy prediction, complementing genomic profiling in precision oncology.

records.title: 3D models to capture and perturb tumour heterogeneity in vitro
records.description: Tumour heterogeneity drives disease progression yet remains difficult to capture in experimental systems. In this Review, Fomina and McGuigan discuss how emerging 3D tumour models, including organoids, assembloids and microfluidic platforms, recapitulate distinct dimensions of tumour heterogeneity to enable mechanistic studies of cancer biology and drug response. They also outline future directions for improving model fidelity, scalability and translational utility.

records.title: Origins and heterogeneity of colorectal cancer
records.description: This Review by Sphyris et al. discusses how the cell-of-origin determines the route of colorectal carcinogenesis and how phenotypic plasticity and heterogeneity shape tumour evolution, disease recurrence, metastatic competence and response to therapy.

records.title: Astrocytes drive stroke-induced glioma progression
records.description: Ye et al. show that ischaemic stroke can drive glioma progression through microenvironmental remodelling of tumour-associated astrocytes.

records.title: Single-cell tumour phylogenetics
records.description: Single-cell sequencing has transformed the study of tumour evolution by enabling high-resolution reconstruction of cancer phylogenies. This Review discusses the models, assumptions and computational approaches underlying single-cell tumour phylogeny inference, and it highlights emerging applications in cancer biology, patient stratification and evolutionary forecasting.

records.title: Hit the pause button
records.description: In a recent study, García-Gómez et al. identify an adaptive proliferative pause program that supports the survival of micrometastatic cells during early brain colonization and uncover therapeutic opportunities to target this state.

records.title: Cancer theranostics
records.description: Theranostics integrates diagnostic imaging with targeted therapy to enhance cancer treatment. In this Review, Sofias et al. discuss recent advances in radiotheranostic strategies, advances in nanotheranostic and microtheranostic platforms, and image-guided therapeutic and surgical interventions in oncology.

records.title: Lean, mean, breast cancer-fighting machine
records.description: Obesity is a modifiable risk factor associated with increased tumour incidence and aggressiveness. Curtin et al. identify an oxylipin secreted by lean adipocytes that suppresses breast cancer progression.

records.title: The urgent challenge of gastroesophageal cancer
records.description: Gastric and oesophageal cancers caused more than 1 million deaths worldwide in 2024. In this Comment, Cancer Grand Challenges explain how they have launched two targeted challenges to address this unmet need, inviting global interdisciplinary teams to apply for up to US $34 million in funding from the Torrey Coast Foundation and Cancer Research UK and move the dial towards the prevention of gastroesophageal cancer.

records.title: Mapping the functional dark proteome in cancer
records.description: The dark proteome encompasses previously undiscovered and uncharacterized protein molecules derived from alternative genomic loci or altered RNA translation. In this Perspective, Prensner et al. describe the current understanding of the dark proteome and set out the critical questions that need to be addressed in the field to determine whether the dark proteome can fulfill its potential for clinical translation.

records.title: Boosting CAR T cell efficacy in cancer with metabolic insights from design to diet
records.description: Although chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has advanced the treatment of many cancers, it is now apparent that metabolism is a major determinant of CAR T cell fitness, persistence and function. Here, Morgan, MacPherson and Lum examine how metabolism integrates with CAR T cell design, outline possible metabolic engineering solutions, and highlight opportunities to leverage diet to improve CAR T cell efficacy in people with haematological cancers.

records.title: Supercentenarians’ superpower to suppress cancer
records.description: Hashimoto et al. show that individuals who have lived to be 110 or older, known as supercentenarians, possess a high fraction of CD4 + cytotoxic T cells, which may contribute to the suppression of subclinical tumours.

records.title: Engineered models of metastasis
records.description: In a recent study, Chramiec, Baldassarri, Öztürk et al. develop a vascularized human multi-tissue platform that captures organ-specific metastatic colonization, microenvironmental remodelling and tumour-cell adaptation, offering a configurable system for modelling metastatic progression.

records.title: Psychosocial burden in cancer survivors
records.description: As health systems struggle to provide follow-up care for the growing number of cancer survivors, the psychosocial consequences of a cancer diagnosis remain insufficiently recognized and addressed. In this Comment, Patricia Ganz explores how survivorship care can better address the long-term psychosocial needs of cancer survivors.

records.title: From blunt-force treatment to precision: 25 years of transformation in cancer research
records.description: This Editorial marks the 25th anniversary of Nature Reviews Cancer . On this milestone we contemplate how our view of cancer has changed over the past 25 years and speculate on what the future holds.

records.title: Replication stress in cancer: origins, consequences and therapeutic opportunities
records.description: Replication stress drives genomic instability, tumour evolution and therapeutic adaptation, yet also creates exploitable vulnerabilities. In this Review, Chen and Zou discuss how chronic replication stress shapes cancer biology and how emerging therapies are targeting the pathways that enable tumour cells to survive it.

records.title: Viral mimicry escape as a necessary feature of malignant transformation
records.description: Viral mimicry is the activation of antiviral immune responses by endogenous nucleic acids that have accumulated in the cytosol. In this Review, Chen et al. highlight how cancer-associated epigenetic and transcriptional dysregulation promotes the generation of immunogenic nucleic acids, which can limit tumour progression. They further outline the mechanisms tumours use to suppress these responses, and the evidence that escape from viral mimicry is central to tumour evolution and a potential target for therapy.

records.title: Making breast cancer innovation deliver for every woman
records.description: Despite remarkable advances in our understanding of breast cancer biology and in the diagnosis and treatment of the disease, outcomes remain deeply influenced by where people live, how health systems function and whether care pathways are effectively coordinated. In this Comment, Miriam Mutebi outlines how we can translate innovation into equitable patient benefits.

records.title: A guide to understanding tumour evolution through the lens of population genetics
records.description: Population genetics provides a quantitative framework for interpreting cancer genomes as records of tumour evolution. This Review outlines how models of mutation, selection and drift enable inference of tumour dynamics from sequencing data, distinguish genetic and non-genetic processes, and support extraction of evolutionary trajectories beyond pattern-based statistical genomics.

records.title: Reflecting on 25 years of cancer research: transformative advances and unmet expectations
records.description: To mark the 25th anniversary of Nature Reviews Cancer , six researchers reflect on the conceptual advances that have reshaped cancer research — from somatic mosaicism, functional genomics and cancer stem cells to tumour metabolism, precision oncology and artificial intelligence — and consider which ideas transformed the field, which fell short of expectations, and what challenges remain.

records.title: A single-cell lens into the co-evolution of genotypes and phenotypes in cancer
records.description: In this Review, Izzo et al. discuss how single-cell multimodal sequencing enables genotype–phenotype mapping and, when combined with phylogenetic reconstruction, provide insights into clonal evolution, cell state plasticity, and cancer progression, revealing mutant-specific vulnerabilities and offering a framework to study somatic evolution across pre-malignant and malignant human tissues.

records.title: Neutrophils in cancer
records.description: Neutrophils exhibit context-dependent pro-tumour and antitumour functions in cancer. In this Review, Diehl, Basto et al. examine neutrophil roles in tumour progression and metastasis, drawing parallels with non-cancer contexts and highlight emerging strategies to therapeutically target and reprogramme neutrophil biology in cancer.

records.title: The next 25 years of cancer research: emerging perspectives and priorities
records.description: To mark the 25th anniversary of Nature Reviews Cancer , six emerging cancer researchers share their perspectives on the future of the field, highlighting conceptual opportunities, challenging established paradigms and identifying the approaches they believe will drive progress in the field over the next 25 years.

records.title: Expanding the reach of menin inhibitors
records.description: Megakaryocytes contribute substantially to the pathogenesis of myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), but therapeutic strategies targeting this lineage are lacking. Wen, Cotton et al. demonstrate that menin inhibition impairs megakaryocyte differentiation, suppresses myelofibrosis and improves disease features across preclinical MPN models.

records.title: The long return on discovery science in cancer therapeutics
records.description: Many advances in cancer treatment depend on discoveries made decades earlier. In this Comment, Murphy et al. discuss the histories of EGFR, HER2, CDK4/6 and RAS, highlighting how long translation can take and how clinical benefit can continue to accumulate as more effective drugs are developed, used in earlier disease settings and combined with existing treatments.

records.title: Early evidence of the carcinogenic effects of e-cigarette use
records.description: In this Journal Club, Yolanda Chirino and Estefany Medina-Reyes discuss a study that used mechanistic markers of carcinogenesis to provide early evidence of the potential cancer risks associated with e-cigarette exposure.

records.title: Shaping the future of early-onset colorectal cancer prevention
records.description: Early-onset colorectal cancer is rising globally. This Roadmap examines current knowledge gaps in risk factors, proposes an integrative conceptual model for risk factor discovery and prevention, and highlights the role of transdisciplinary science and patient engagement in reversing the trend.

records.title: Origins and consequences of oncogenic 3D chromatin remodelling
records.description: In this Review, Franceschini and colleagues discuss how remodelling of the 3D structure of chromatin in cancer is both a cause and a consequence of genetic and epigenetic alterations and highlight how chromatin 3D conformation might be exploited for diagnosis and therapy.

records.title: Brain barriers at the crossroads of glioma immune surveillance and immunotherapy response
records.description: Immunotherapy remains largely ineffective in gliomas despite success in other cancers. In this Review, Engelhardt and Platten outline how central nervous system immune privilege is enforced by specialized brain barriers that restrict T cell surveillance and discuss strategies to overcome these barriers to improve T cell-based immunotherapy for glioma.

records.title: Epigenetic changes linked to cell replication connect ageing with cancer risk
records.description: In this Journal Club, Sandra Romero-Cordoba discusses a study that identifies a replication-associated DNA methylation signature, termed CellDRIFT, providing evidence that epigenetic drift linked to cell division may contribute to oncogenic transformation.

records.title: An early shot at stopping PDAC
records.description: The progression of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) from precursor lesions presents an opportunity for cancer prevention. Haldar et al. developed mKRAS-VAX, a peptide vaccine targeting six common KRAS mutations in PDAC, and evaluated it in a phase I clinical trial.

records.title: Accelerated ageing confers early-onset cancer risk
records.description: Tian et al. conducted an observational cohort study utilizing data from biobanks in the UK and USA, finding that more advanced biological ageing compared to chronological age may be a risk factor for early-onset solid cancers with implications for cancer prevention and early interception.

records.title: Converging engineered models of cancer and artificial intelligence
records.description: No existing model can reliably predict how an individual cancer will evolve. In this Comment, Guimarães and Reis argue that the future of precision oncology lies not in increasingly sophisticated in vitro tumour models or in artificial intelligence alone, but in the iterative feedback loop between the two.

records.title: The DNA damage response and cancer immunotherapy
records.description: In this Review, Hong and Li explore how defects in DNA damage response (DDR) pathways shape tumour immunogenicity and influence responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors. They highlight shared immunological consequences across distinct DDR alterations, discuss mechanisms of resistance and evaluate therapeutic strategies integrating DDR-targeting agents with immunotherapy to improve clinical outcomes.

records.title: Who gets told what is impossible?
records.description: Twenty-five years after the launch of Nature Reviews Cancer , the experiences of women in cancer research have changed in important ways, with gains in visibility, representation and recognition. In this World View, Joyce reflects on the progress achieved and the persistent structural barriers that continue to impede equity.

records.title: Igniting antitumour immunity with cancer cell pyroptosis
records.description: In this Review, Liu et al. discuss how pyroptosis, executed by a family of pore-forming proteins known as gasdermins, can induce antitumour immunity, which might be therapeutically leveraged for synergy with existing cancer immunotherapies.

records.title: A viral coding circRNA contributes to HPV-driven oncogenesis
records.description: In this Journal Club, Muñoz-Bello and Lizano discuss the discovery of circE7, a protein-coding circular RNA generated by back-splicing in high-risk HPV that drives E7 expression and tumour growth, revealing a previously unappreciated mechanism of viral oncogene regulation.

records.title: Cuproptosis promotes antitumour immunity
records.description: In a recent study, Lei, Lu, Xu et al. identify cuproptosis as a form of immunogenic cell death that stimulates adaptive antitumour immunity. In turn, CD8⁺ T cell-derived IFNγ enhances tumour sensitivity to cuproptosis through STAT1–IRF1–FDX1 signalling, establishing a reciprocal immunometabolic circuit with important implications for cancer immunotherapy.

records.title: GABA takes the edge off anti-tumour immunity
records.description: Glioblastoma exhibits sex-specific differences in disease progression, incidence and immune regulation. Now, Pathak et al. identify GABA (γ-aminobutyric acid) as a key driver of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cell-mediated glioblastoma progression in women.

records.title: Escaping the trap
records.description: A recent study identifies TEX264-dependent nucleophagy as an important mechanism that mediates the clearance of trapped PARP1, thereby limiting PARP1-induced toxicity and promoting resistance to PARP inhibitors.

records.title: A genomic and epigenomic lens into the biology of acute lymphoblastic leukaemia
records.description: In this Review, Iacobucci and Mullighan discuss how advances in genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of acute lymphoblastic leukaemia have revealed molecular heterogeneity, lineage plasticity and mechanisms of treatment resistance in both B cell and T cell disease, thereby refining risk stratification and informing therapeutic decision-making.

records.title: Systemic health impact of cancer-associated extracellular vesicles and particles
records.description: In this Review, Wang et al. describe how extracellular vesicles and particles contribute to the systemic effects of cancer by providing a form of intercellular communication between tumours and the host through the transfer of bioactive cargo to recipient cells. These systemic effects include immune dysregulation in pre-metastatic niches, thrombosis and cardiovascular disease, liver metabolic dysfunction, glucose metabolism disorders and cachexia, suggesting that holistic approaches to cancer treatment are necessary to simultaneously target the tumour and its multi-organ paraneoplastic effects.

records.title: CLIM-TIME links tumour genetics to spatial immune architecture
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade, Weiwei Hu describes the development and use of CLIM-TIME, a scalable in vivo platform that integrates CRISPR perturbation screens with spatially resolved transcriptomic and immune profiling to link tumour-intrinsic genetic alterations to distinct immune microenvironments.

records.title: Imaging the hallmarks of cancer
records.description: In this Review, Grimm et al. describe the range of non-invasive diagnostic imaging approaches to monitor the various hallmarks of cancer and how their implementation is shaping clinical practice.

records.title: Serving sulfur to boost anti-tumour immunity
records.description: Gut microbiome composition and metabolite profiles have previously been linked to both colorectal tumorigenesis and immune checkpoint inhibitor responsiveness. Now, Lobel et al. identify sulfur amino acid metabolism as a microorganism-derived metabolic pathway that enhances anti-tumour immunity.

records.title: How to give a bad talk
records.description: Effective presentations require clarity and audience awareness. In this Comment, Itai Yanai outlines common misconceptions about presentations and how to address them to deliver more impactful and insightful talks.

records.title: Beyond oncogenesis: the unexplored benefits of viruses in cancer immunity
records.description: The study of tumour virology has traditionally focused on oncogenic viruses and their associated mechanisms of cancer initiation and promotion. Yet certain viral exposures can be beneficial by enhancing antitumour immunity. In this Review, Wang et al. explore the increasingly emerging evidence of protective roles of viruses in cancer immunity and how this knowledge could be harnessed to develop a virome-guided framework for cancer immunoprevention.

records.title: 3D multi-omics tumour atlases: from technology to biology and clinical translation
records.description: In this Review, Liu et al. describe the established and emerging tools for the generation of comprehensive 3D tumour atlases, the analysis of which has the potential to uncover novel biomarkers for risk stratification, early detection, preventive interventions, and transformative diagnostic and treatment strategies.

records.title: AACR 2026
records.description: The 2026 annual meeting of the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) was held under the theme ‘Precision, Partnership, Purpose: Advancing Cancer Science to Save Lives Globally’. Here, we summarize some key highlights from the meeting.

records.title: PRISM enables accurate microbial discovery in cancer genomics
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Bassel Ghaddar describes the development of PRISM, an efficient computational pipeline for microbial species detection and decontamination from genomic sequencing data, enabling the study of microbial associations with cancer.

records.title: Detection of cytokine-responsive cells using CyCLoPs
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Guangqing Lu describes the development and use of cytokine cellular locating platforms (CyCLoPs), a technology that enables visualization and tracking of cytokine signalling in vivo.

records.title: Mutation-centric kinase drug repurposing for rare cancers
records.description: Rare cancers remain underserved by precision oncology, in part because many oncogenic variants lack matched therapies despite a growing arsenal of targeted drugs. In this Comment, the authors propose that systematic, variant-level pharmacological mapping of approved kinase inhibitors can transform this gap into an opportunity for scalable drug repurposing.

records.title: An adenosine derivative for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma
records.description: In this Journal Club, Mauricio Díaz-Muñoz discusses a study showing that the adenosine derivative IFC-305 restores mitochondrial structure and bioenergetics while reducing tumour burden in a rat model of hepatocellular carcinoma.

records.title: Structural variants disrupt chromatin architecture
records.description: In this Journal Club, Stephenson-Gussinye and Furlan-Magaril discuss a study exploring how structural variants reshape three-dimensional genome architecture in cancer, explaining why only a subset lead to functional changes in gene expression.

records.title: Message in a vesicle: T cells boost tumour immunity
records.description: Extracellular vesicles have emerged as key modulators of immune responses. Hu et al. show that activated T cells secrete extracellular vesicles that promote antigen presentation in tumour cells and dendritic cells, thereby enhancing immune-mediated tumour clearance.

records.title: Beat it!
records.description: The heart is strikingly resistant to tumour formation despite its rich vascularization. In a recent study, Ciucci, Lorizio et al. identify mechanical load as a key barrier, showing that forces generated by cardiac contraction activate a mechano-epigenetic pathway that suppresses cancer cell proliferation in vivo and in engineered heart tissues.

records.title: Beyond sex determination: the Y chromosome in male cancers
records.description: This Review by Abdel-Hafiz et al. describes the current and emerging evidence that loss of the Y chromosome is linked to susceptibility, progression and poor outcomes in multiple cancer types, as well as its potential use as a biomarker for prognosis and precision therapy.

records.title: Mesenchymal stromal/stem cells in tumour initiation, progression and therapy
records.description: Mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (MSCs) influence tumour initiation, progression and immune modulation across diverse cancer types. In this Review, Garcia et al. outline how tissue-dependent and context-dependent MSC plasticity underlies their tumour-supportive or tumour-restraining functions and highlight emerging mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities that position MSC biology as a promising avenue for cancer treatment.

records.title: Tracing disease origin with plasma cell-free chromatin
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Xiaoxuan Meng describes the development of cf-EpiTracing, a highly sensitive and automated epigenetic liquid-biopsy platform that captures histone modifications on cell-free chromatin from plasma, enabling unbiased monitoring of cancer.

records.title: Regulation of immune checkpoint molecules in cancer immune evasion and therapy
records.description: Tumours evade immunity by dynamically rewiring immune checkpoint expression across multiple regulatory layers. In this Review, Eris, Zu et al. synthesize how these mechanisms operate in tumour and immune cells, connect them to therapeutic resistance, and highlight emerging biomarkers and therapeutic strategies that target convergent regulatory nodes to improve immunotherapy outcomes.

records.title: Remembering inflammation increases cancer risk
records.description: Colitis predisposes to colorectal cancer, but how inflammation promotes tumour initiation has remained unclear. Nagaraja et al. show that inflammatory injury imprints a heritable epigenetic memory in colonic stem cells that enhances AP-1-driven proliferative programs and accelerates malignant outgrowth following oncogenic mutation.

records.title: Stem cells as an essential mediator of the exercise–tumorigenesis link
records.description: Aerobic exercise influences physiology and generally reduces cancer risk, yet the mechanisms connecting these effects remain incompletely understood. In this Perspective, Zhuang and colleagues outline a model in which exercise-induced physiological adaptation regulates adult stem cell behaviour in ways that limit transformation and tumour initiation.

records.title: Microplastics but macro-concerns on the brain
records.description: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly recognized as pervasive environmental exposures. Li et al. analysed human brain tumour samples and post-mortem healthy brain tissue to quantify MNP burden, and characterize particle composition and spatial distribution.

records.title: The sleeping threat: targeting cancer dormancy to transform metastasis therapy
records.description: This Review synthesizes emerging insights into how microenvironmental cues, epigenetic programmes and immune interactions govern disseminated cancer cell dormancy and outlines how advances in dormancy research could guide the development of biomarkers and therapies to prevent metastatic relapse.

records.title: Enhancer and metabolic rewiring by KMT2C–COMPASS or KMT2D–COMPASS family loss in cancer creates druggable vulnerabilities
records.description: In this Review, Zhao and Shilatifard examine how mutations in components of the KMT2C-containing or KMT2D-containing COMPASS complex drive cancer progression and discuss therapeutic approaches targeting epigenetic, metabolic, immune and DNA repair vulnerabilities arising from this altered COMPASS activity.

records.title: Context-dependent synthetic lethality — an emerging precision therapeutic approach
records.description: In this Review, Chang et al. discuss context-dependent synthetic lethality whereby various genetic contexts produce cancer-intrinsic vulnerabilities and provide a framework that evaluates and considers therapeutic index to enable the translation of synthetic lethality into more selective and durable cancer therapies.

records.title: Cancer risk in children with congenital anomalies
records.description: The established link between congenital anomalies and cancer could lead to improved surveillance and therapeutic strategies. However, we must first expand population-based studies to confirm these patterns, along with detailed molecular assessments to identify risk markers and deeper patient profiling to support precision medicine.

records.title: Advancing AI for multi-omics and clinical data integration in basic and translational cancer research
records.description: While high-throughput omics have deepened our understanding of tumour complexity, analyses restricted to a single omics layer risk overlooking key dimensions of biological regulation. In this Review, Liu and colleagues highlight how artificial intelligence could be harnessed for integrating multi-omics data to provide patient-specific insights into cancer mechanisms and treatment response.

records.title: Microbiota and immune-related adverse events in cancer immunotherapy
records.description: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) complicate cancer immunotherapy, necessitating cancer treatment cessation and management of irAEs. In this Progress article, Schneider et al. highlight the role of the microbiome in driving irAE development and progression, particularly immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated colitis, through clinical and preclinical evidence, emphasizing immune and microbial interactions while discussing potential therapeutic strategies to mitigate risks.

records.title: vCATCH enables body-wide in vivo drug distribution mapping
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Zhengyuan Pang describes the development and use of volumetric clearing-assisted tissue click chemistry (vCATCH), a pipeline that enables mapping of covalent drug binding at cellular resolution across a mouse body.

records.title: The versatile interplay between steatotic liver disease and liver cancer
records.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and alcoholic liver disease (ALD) are drivers of liver cancer, promoting its development through chronic liver injury and inflammation. In this Review, Rahbari et al. highlight the distinct pathophysiological mechanisms of progression and therapeutic advancements for MASLD and ALD, emphasizing the need for more tailored approaches to manage these complex diseases and their cancer risks.

records.title: Rethinking ovarian cancer III: the past decade and future directions
records.description: In this Expert Recommendation, Bowtell and colleagues outline progress made over the last decade in the research and treatment of high-grade serous carcinoma as well as current challenges and research priorities for the coming years to reduce incidence and improve patient outcomes.

records.title: Kill three birds with one stone
records.description: In a recent study, Gudenas et al. map pineoblastoma subgroups to pinealocyte progenitors and identify a shared photoreceptor-like transcriptional network across pineoblastoma, retinoblastoma and group 3 medulloblastoma, revealing a developmental vulnerability with therapeutic potential.

records.title: A fatty competitor in tumour immunity
records.description: Adipose tissue and adipocytes have been implicated in promoting tumour progression and hindering anti-tumour immunity. Wang et al. investigated the functional role of tumour-associated visceral adipose tissue in regulating colorectal cancer anti-tumour immunity and immunotherapy efficacy.

records.title: Targeting shared neoantigens in solid tumours
records.description: In this Journal Club, Terrazas and Peón discuss a study that identifies a recurrent CTNNB1 mutation that generates shared neoantigens amenable to engineered T cell receptor (TCR)-T cell recognition. The work demonstrates potent antitumour activity across models and highlights the potential of targeting public mutations to broaden TCR-T cell immunotherapy for solid tumours.

records.title: AI-driven smart patient retrieval for precision oncology
records.description: Tumour boards are often constrained by time-intensive data preparation and discussion. In this Comment, Wang and Chaudhari advocate for the use of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven smart patient-retrieval systems to facilitate more informed and individualized clinical decision-making.

records.title: Functional m 6 A site detection by FOCAS
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yifan Zhang describes the development and use of FOCAS, a platform for site-specific, transcriptome-wide mapping of functional m 6 A RNA modifications, revealing widespread intra-transcript functional diversity and uncovering epitranscriptomic and epigenomic interactions that shape cancer cell fitness.

records.title: Striking the right balance with type I interferon signalling in cancer
records.description: Type I interferons (IFNs) critically influence cancer development, progression and therapeutic response. In this Review, Parker, Haynes and colleagues explore the complexity of IFN signalling, with a particular focus on tumour-intrinsic mechanisms, and outline strategies for reprogramming IFN activity in tumours to enhance anticancer immunity and improve patient outcomes.

records.title: Avoiding cancer through collective behaviour
records.description: In this Journal Club, Rodríguez-Lelis and Gómez-Schiavon discuss a study that challenges the oncogene-induced senescence paradigm and proposes that cooperative, feedback-driven growth arrest better explains growth dynamics in BRAF-mutant benign nevi.

records.title: Metabolic vulnerability in fusion-driven ependymoma
records.description: In a recent study published in Nature , Natarajan et al. uncover a metabolic–epigenetic circuit in which glutamine-derived itaconate functions as an oncometabolite to sustain oncogenic ZFTA–RELA expression in ependymoma. Disrupting this pathway lowers ZFTA–RELA levels and suppresses tumour growth in preclinical models, revealing a promising therapeutic vulnerability in this aggressive cancer.

records.title: Re-routing IgE for cancer therapy
records.description: In a study published in Cell , Xu et al. show that mast cells engineered with tumour-antigen specific antibodies and loaded with an oncolytic virus can be activated by antigen encounter to drive targeted tumour cell killing and amplify local anti-tumour immunity.

records.title: Claudin proteins as emerging therapeutic targets for solid tumours
records.description: In this Review, Saviano et al. explore the frequent deregulation of claudins (CLDNs) in solid tumours and highlight their role in cancer progression. They discuss strategies to target CLDNs by exploiting tumour-specific surface expression or inhibiting oncogenic signalling and outline knowledge gaps, challenges and opportunities for advancing CLDN-directed cancer therapies.

records.title: The intestinal microbiota as a key modulator of acute graft-versus-host disease
records.description: In this Review, Paredes et al. discuss preclinical and clinical evidence suggesting that the intestinal microbiome influences outcomes of allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation and, in particular, graft-versus-host disease and propose that microbiota-focused approaches may improve these clinical outcomes.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-generated synthetic data for cancer research and clinical trials
records.description: Synthetic data generated by generative artificial intelligence models can serve as a substitute for real patient data. In this Review, Eckardt et al. discuss how synthetic data sets can overcome barriers to data access and sharing, democratize scientific discovery in cancer research, and reduce the costs and failure rates of cancer clinical trials. They also discuss how this will only become possible if we can overcome the challenges of a lack of standardization in training data selection, model evaluation, bias mitigation, privacy preservation and quality assurance.

records.title: Decoding cancer across scales with metabolomics
records.description: In this Review, Rowles and Patti present metabolomics workflows to study cancer across scales. They explore the nutrient demands of cancer cells and how those needs can be fulfilled through metabolic interactions within the tumour microenvironment or systemic crosstalk with distant tissues, and discuss the opportunities and challenges of each approach and offer insights into future research directions.

records.title: Inherited resilience
records.description: Mutant haematopoietic stem cells display broad fitness variation, suggesting that protective mechanisms may limit clonal expansion and malignant transformation. Now, Agarwal et al. identify a germline noncoding variant that confers resilience to clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) by dampening expression of the RNA-binding protein MSI2.

records.title: Carboplatin trains macrophages for cardiac defence
records.description: In a recent Science Immunology paper, He et al. show that treatment with the chemotherapy carboplatin reshapes cardiac-resident macrophage populations, protecting against later heart disease.

records.title: l -Fucose: a dietary sugar with multifaceted potential in the biology and therapy of cancer
records.description: The conjugation of glycoproteins and glycolipids with the dietary sugar L -fucose is known as fucosylation. In this Progress article, Bitaraf et al. describe the latest work showing how fucosylation is deregulated in cancer, influencing tumour progression and therapeutic responses, and how it might be leveraged to treat cancer.

records.title: Cat viruses as windows into human oncogenesis
records.description: Oncogenic viruses cause 15% of all human cancers. Cats, which are naturally susceptible to cancers caused by feline homologues of human tumour viruses, represent an opportunity to develop treatment and prevention strategies for viral cancers using comparative oncology. Increased investment in this approach could benefit both pets and people.

records.title: Radiation as an immune modulator: mechanisms and implications for combination with immunotherapy
records.description: Radiation therapy induces immune responses both systemically and within the tumour microenvironment. In this Review, Darragh and Karam present preclinical and clinical evidence to highlight this complex interplay and outline strategies to enhance the immunogenic potential of radiation therapy to improve both therapeutic efficacy and patient outcomes.

records.title: Tumour explants as next-generation models of cancer
records.description: To preserve tumour architecture, cellular heterogeneity and the dynamic crosstalk that influences cancer, Fong and colleagues advocate for coordinated, cross-disciplinary and sustained efforts to promote the widespread adoption of tumour explants.

records.title: The rise of spatial insights into tumour tissue architecture
records.description: In this Journal Club, Siliceo and Rodríguez discuss a study that presents histoCAT, an interactive toolbox for spatial biology that combines image-based visualization with unsupervised cellular neighborhood analysis to uncover tissue architecture and cell–cell interactions.

records.title: Heterocellular crosstalk and architecture of the pancreatic tumour microenvironment
records.description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is defined by a fibroinflammatory microenvironment, which influences both disease progression and therapy response. In this Review, Arnold et al. outline our current understanding of the complex interplay between the stromal elements of the tumour microenvironment in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and present ways we might use this knowledge to develop better therapeutic strategies for patients with pancreatic cancer.

records.title: Artificial intelligence agents in cancer research and oncology
records.description: Artificial intelligence agents are autonomous systems that use large language models to reason and as such can perform complex, multistep tasks with minimal human oversight. This Review by Truhn et al. discusses how these agents — which have already been implemented in several industries — could transform cancer research and oncology, and looks at the challenges that need to be addressed before they can be efficiently and safely used.

records.title: When the time is right
records.description: In a study published in Nature , Lourenço et al. demonstrate that strong oncogenic driver mutations undergo negative selection unless they occur in a permissive tissue context.

records.title: Opportunities and challenges of targeting cGAS–STING in cancer
records.description: In this Review, Lu et al. discuss the dual role of the cyclic guanosine monophosphate–adenosine monophosphate synthase (cGAS)–stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway in cancer, emphasizing its involvement in both tumour suppression and promotion. They highlight the diverse sources of pathway activation and suggest that this functional duality may underlie the limited clinical success of cGAS–STING targeting in cancer therapy.

records.title: Double trouble for the tumour glycocode
records.description: By incorporating lectins that target specific tumour-associated carbohydrate antigens, Zhou et al. engineered bispecific antibodies that induce effective T cell activation and tumour regression in various cancers.

records.title: Convergence of machine learning and genomics for precision oncology
records.description: In this Perspective, Reardon et al. explore how integrating machine learning into next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based molecular diagnostic workflows can enhance precision oncology. They discuss the benefits, challenges and responsible implementation of these approaches, highlighting their potential to streamline variant interpretation, maximize clinical insights and support more informed decision-making at the point-of-care.
